facts.text: Finland is an autonomous Grand Duchy within the Russian Empire. Swedish-era laws and much of the inherited social order remain important foundations of administration.
The Finnish markka is the monetary unit.
Finland adopted the gold standard in 1878.
Elementary schools exist under the 1866 school reform, but schooling is not yet compulsory and rural school provision remains uneven.
Ordinary farm work is still heavily dependent on human labour, draft animals and hand tools rather than modern agricultural machinery.
Rural daily life is less governed by modern minute-by-minute standardized clock time; daylight, meals, work tasks, bells and local practice matter strongly to the shape of the day.
November is a transition into thermal winter across much of Finland. Rain, sleet, snow, thaw and freeze can all plausibly occur, and permanent snow cover need not yet be established.
The growing season is ending or over, so rural work shifts away from active field growth toward livestock care, stored produce, fuel, repairs, transport and winter preparation.
Long winter evenings can bring several household activities into the same indoor space; reading aloud may accompany handicrafts and other domestic work.
